title: Sale in a wallet user interface
scope: e2e/wallet-ui/ runs two targets from the patched starter wallet. The default target sells 1 USDT or 0.0001 ETH on Sepolia. --target production-polygon sells the given USDT amount on Polygon against the production API [ref 2] and binds the runner protocol to environment production [ref 3]. The runner reads the transaction list [ref 0] and keeps the row whose inputTxId is that hash [ref 1]. It does not send the hash in that request. The chain transfer, the wallet send and that recognition are executed. On the default target the entries are the stand-ins around them, except the bank payout, which is switched off. --target production-polygon uses the production API and the account holder's saved bank account [ref 4]; the patched wallet, Maestro, the simulator and the switched-off bank payout remain.

entries.status: fake — patched starter, not the released wallet
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] points Ethereum at @tetherto/wdk-wallet-evm instead of @tetherto/wdk-wallet-evm-7702-gasless. [ref 1] removes the Ethereum bundler and paymaster URLs. [ref 2] adds Sell. [ref 3] opens the sell page in a WebView and does not inject a provider. [ref 4] shows an Ethereum token fee in ETH and does not add it to the token total. [ref 5] adds the confirm test id on the send review button. [ref 6] adds Sell ETH.
entries.insteadOf: the unmodified released WDK starter wallet, with Ethereum on the gasless package
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove the sale in an unpatched or released wallet.

entries.status: mixed — sandbox on the default target, the production API on production-polygon
entries.mechanism: The default target reads https://dev.api.dfx.swiss [ref 0] and binds the starter's DFX protocol to environment sandbox [ref 1]. --target production-polygon reads the production API [ref 2] and binds the runner protocol to environment production [ref 3].
entries.insteadOf: On the default target, the production DFX API at https://api.dfx.swiss. --target production-polygon uses that API and is not a stand-in.
entries.doesNotProve: A green default-target run does not prove that production recognizes the deposit or books the sale. A green --target production-polygon run does not prove the sandbox.

entries.status: mixed — invented per run on the default target, the saved account on production-polygon
entries.mechanism: On the default target [ref 0] builds a Swiss IBAN. The BBAN starts with clearing 00000 and twelve random digits, and the two check digits are 98 minus the mod-97 remainder of the BBAN followed by 121700. --target production-polygon reads the account holder's active bank account [ref 1] and never invents an IBAN.
entries.insteadOf: On the default target, an IBAN of a bank account the seller holds. --target production-polygon uses that saved account and is not a stand-in.
entries.doesNotProve: A green default-target run does not prove that a bank would accept the invented number or pay the sale to an account the seller holds. A green --target production-polygon run does not prove a payout to an invented IBAN.

entries.status: switched off — the runner stops at PayoutInProgress or Completed
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] checks the booked payout and returns when the sale row is PayoutInProgress or Completed. The runner does not read a bank debit.
entries.insteadOf: a bank transfer of the fiat amount to the payout account
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that a bank paid the fiat amount.
